title: State and Society up to 1000 CE

topics.title: The Vedic period: sources and political institutions
topics.ncert_sections: The Beginnings; State and Administration: The Vedic Period; Political Institutions in the Vedic Period

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the four Vedas and the parts of Vedic texts and explain why historians use them as sources.
Describe the role of the raja, the janas and the assemblies sabha, samiti and vidhata in early Vedic polity.

topics.title: Janapadas, mahajanapadas and early kingdoms
topics.ncert_sections: Let's Analyse; Early Kingdoms and Republics

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the shift from kin-based janas to territorial janapadas and mahajanapadas, and the forms of polity that followed.
Relate iron tools, wider crop variety and NBPW pottery to the growth of the Ganga plains.
Identify the early kingdoms of Tamilakam and their emblems.

topics.title: Duties and ideals of the king and the council of ministers
topics.ncert_sections: Duties and Ideals of the King; Council of Ministers

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the limits on royal authority and the ideal of authority over the whole subcontinent (chakravarti kshetra).
Describe Kautilya's seven constituents of the state and why they must work together.
Evaluate how inscriptions such as the Junagadh rock record help historians study administration.
Identify the provincial, district and village units used in northern and southern kingdoms.
Describe the composition of the Gupta district office.
Explain how village assemblies, variyams and the Kudavolai system made villages self-reliant.

topics.title: Ethics: the foundation of law and life
topics.ncert_sections: Ethics: The Foundation of Law and Life

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the principles of samatva and rita as described in early Indian texts.
Explain the meaning of dharma and how ethics guided governance from the Mauryas to the Cholas.

topics.title: Varna, jati and social mobility
topics.ncert_sections: Social Structures and Everyday Life: Varna and Jati; Social Mobility

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the origin of the varna idea and why early occupations are described as flexible.
Distinguish jati from varna and identify the factors that led to the growth of jatis.
Use inscriptions as evidence of social and occupational mobility.

topics.title: Family, women, religious life and education
topics.ncert_sections: Family and Society; Role of Women; Religious Life and the Emergence of Bhakti; The Quest for Knowledge

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the four ashramas and the four purusharthas.
Describe the roles of women in Vedic, Gupta-Vakataka, Sangam and Chola times.
Explain the rise of Bhakti in the Tamil region and its open, ritual-free path.

topics.title: Economy: agriculture, irrigation, trade and guilds
topics.ncert_sections: Economy: Agriculture and Land Revenue; Irrigation; Trade: Trade Routes and Ports; Guilds

concepts.learning_objective: Explain land revenue and the state's role in building irrigation works.
Identify the major land routes and ports that linked early Indian trade.
Analyse the economic and banking role of guilds using inscriptional evidence.
